title: Chunking: how to cut documents
hook: A chunk is what the search can return. Cut it badly and everything after it suffers.
inPlainWords: A chunk is one piece of a document that search can hand back. Too small and it loses context. Too big and the match gets watered down.

useCase.title: A returns-policy PDF with headings, lists and a fee table
useCase.story: Search should return the exact rule with enough context to be understood, including the table row that gives the restocking fee.

approaches.name: Fixed size
approaches.what: Cut every N characters, no matter what.
approaches.greatWhen: Uniform plain text and a quick start.
approaches.avoidWhen: Structured documents. It cuts sentences and tables in half.

approaches.name: By paragraph or sentence
approaches.what: Split where the writing naturally breaks.
approaches.avoidWhen: Long sections whose heading carries the meaning.

approaches.name: By structure
approaches.what: Follow the document's own outline: headings, sections and tables.
approaches.example: Each heading with its content is one chunk, and tables stay whole.

approaches.name: Overlap
approaches.what: Repeat the end of one chunk at the start of the next.

approaches.name: Small to find, big to read
approaches.what: Search on small chunks, but hand the model the surrounding section.
approaches.greatWhen: You need precise matching and full context.
approaches.example: Match one sentence, then send its whole section.

approaches.name: Add metadata
approaches.what: Tag each chunk with product, date and document type so you can filter.
approaches.example: Only search Returns documents updated this year.

challenge.question: Which chunking keeps the fee table intact and gives useful context?

options.why: It will cut the table apart.

options.text: By heading, tables kept whole, small overlap, plus metadata
options.why: It follows the document's meaning and lets you filter by date and type.
Too big. Matches get watered down and prompts get huge.

options.text: Sentence chunks, but send the surrounding section to the model
options.why: A strong technique, but more setup than this simple document needs.

bestCase.title: Structure-aware chunks with metadata
bestCase.example: The "Opened electronics" chunk keeps its heading and the whole fee table. Metadata says doc=Returns, updated=this month. A question about restocking fees returns that chunk, complete.

worstCase.title: Blind slicing
worstCase.example: A fixed cut lands between "Restocking fee:" and "10%". One chunk says "Restocking fee:" with no number, and the next starts with "10%" and no label. The bot says "The fee is 15%", which comes from another product line.

steps.label: The PDF
steps.goes: Headings, bullet lists and one fee table.

steps.label: Cut by sections
steps.goes: One chunk per section, and the table stays in one piece.
steps.goesWrong: Blind 500-character cuts split the fee table in two.

steps.label: Index
steps.goes: The chunks are ready for search.

takeaway: Chunk by meaning, not by length. Keep tables whole, and tag chunks so you can filter.
